Have no conflicts in gene impact prediction (structural effects)."
comments:
Conflicting structural effects arise whenever there is an "event" taking place inside either one of such sequences. If there is an important genomic element which has either its START or END inside either of the two sequences, that constitutes an "event". If the element starts inside the sequence, we don't care where it ends; if it ends inside the sequence, we don't care where it starts. That is, there is no event if and only if the sequence is entirely inside (contained by) the element. In the most general sense, "elements" constitute everything that is not a variant.

description: This is a re-implementation of the "PREDICTED_DUP_PARTIAL" annotation from SVAnnotate: "Gene(s) which are partially overlapped by an SV's duplication, but the transcription start site is not duplicated. When the duplication is in tandem, the result is that there is one intact copy of the full endogenous gene."
